Based on your preference for medieval historical fiction featuring political intrigue and warfare, similar to the works of Ken Follett and Bernard Cornwell, here are some highly recommended books:

1. **"The Pillars of the Earth" by Ken Follett**
   Since you already enjoy Follett, this is his most famous work. It is set in 12th-century England and focuses on the building of a cathedral, but it is deeply intertwined with the political struggles, wars, and power dynamics of the time.

2. **"The Last Kingdom" series by Bernard Cornwell**
   If you haven't read this series yet, it is essential. It follows Uhtred of Bebbanburg during the Viking invasions of England. It is renowned for its gritty realism, detailed battle scenes, and complex political maneuvering between Saxons, Danes, and Wessex.

3. **"The Name of the Rose" by Umberto Eco**
   While more of a mystery/thriller, this book is set in a 14th-century Italian monastery. It features intense intellectual and political intrigue, religious conflict, and a dark, atmospheric setting that appeals to fans of complex historical narratives.

4. **"The Hollow Lands" by Mark Chadbourn**
   This series is set in post-Roman Britain (5th century AD). It blends historical fact with myth and magic, but the core remains grounded in the brutal warfare and tribal politics of the era. It offers a different flavor from Cornwell but shares the same focus on conflict and survival.

5. **"The Warlord Chronicles" by Bernard Cornwell**
   This series reimagines the Arthurian legend from a historical perspective. It is set in the late 5th and early 6th centuries, focusing on the transition from Roman Britain to the Saxon invasions. It is rich in military detail and political strategy.

6. **"The Book of the New Sun" by Gene Wolfe**
   While this is science fiction/fantasy, it is often recommended to fans of dense, intricate historical fiction due to its complex narrative structure and deep world-building. However, if you prefer strictly historical settings, consider **"The Saxon Stories" prequel "The Winter King"** by Cornwell, which sets the stage for the main series.
